topic: Loan applications and costs by channel
decision: whether to close the broker channel to cut acquisition costs

columns.funded_value_musd: value of loans paid out, $ millions
columns.acquisition_cost_per_loan_usd: marketing, commission and processing cost per funded loan, US dollars
columns.days_to_fund: median days from application to payout
columns.default_rate_12m_pct: share of loans in default within 12 months, percent
columns.default_rate_basis: actual = observed history, projected = model estimate

findings.text: Online applications grew 34% from January to September.
Branches pay out fastest, in a median of 6 days.
Broker brings 32% of funded loan value from 17% of applications, because broker loans are much larger ($58,000 on average, against $9,000 to $20,000 in the other channels).
Partner-app loans are the smallest, about $9,000 on average.
Approval rates are steady from month to month in every channel.
Broker loans only started in November 2025, so the broker 12-month default rate (2.1%) is a projection, not an observed figure. The same is true of the partner app.
Applications peaked in March, when tax refunds arrive.
Broker is the most expensive channel: about $1,446 to acquire each funded loan, against $820 at branches, $342 online and $259 through the partner app.
The partner app launched in March 2026.
Total funded value over the nine months was $335 million.

main.gist: Broker is costly per loan but brings a large share of loan value

caveat.gist: Broker default rates are projections, not observed

facts.q: What percentage of funded loan value, and what percentage of applications, came from the broker channel?
